subject: lighthouse
pitch: A cozy lighthouse diorama on a tiny rocky island. A red-and-white striped tower with a glowing lantern room and a black iron balcony, a keeper's cottage with a crooked chimney and a blue door, a wooden jetty with a rowboat tied to it, a couple of seagulls, tufts of grass and wildflowers between the rocks, and turquoise water with white foam around the shore, all on a round display base.
reasoning:
I'm uncertain about the exact SDK API details, so I plan to lean on plain three.js geometry where unsure, using the builder minimally with a root joint and attaching plain objects directly, while keeping to the limited flat color palette for materials.

I'm sketching out dimensions for a lighthouse diorama: a wooden base cylinder, a turquoise water ring, and a rocky island built from a flat-shaded dodecahedron with a grassy top, planning rough heights and radii to keep the scene modest and proportioned.

Now I'm detailing the lighthouse tower itself, stacking frustum bands in alternating red and white with a gallery ring, railing posts, a glowing lantern room with black mullions, a conical roof, and a ball finial, plus foam torus rings around the island and jetty. I'm also planning a small cottage with white walls, a dark pyramid roof, a crooked chimney made of offset boxes, and a blue door with glowing windows.

I'm shaping the island top as a flattened cylinder with grass coloring and a rocky skirt, scattering extra rocks near the edges, then building a jetty of plank boxes and posts extending from the island into the water. For the tied rowboat, I'm using a half-sphere hemisphere geometry scaled into an elongated hull shape with red and tan coloring, plus simple seats and a rope line.

Now I'm adding seagulls -- one perched on a jetty post and one flying above, each built from an ellipsoid body, head sphere, orange cone beak, and angled box wings -- along with grass tufts and flowers scattered across the island top using randomized positions that avoid building footprints. I'm working out placement coordinates so the lighthouse, cottage, and jetty don't overlap on the island's base.

I'm adding ripple and foam details around the water's edge using torus shapes and scattered foam blobs, then setting up a reusable mesh helper function for adding geometry with color, position, and rotation. Now I'm building the lighthouse tower itself -- a stone plinth, tapered bands stacked upward, and a gallery with railing posts near the top.

Next I'm adding the lantern room with emissive glass, mullions, and a red conical roof, plus a small point light for glow. Then I'm placing the cottage structure nearby with its own walls, door, and a pyramidal roof made from a scaled cone.
